questions.prompt: Gemini's docs say XML-style tags or Markdown headings both work. What rule do they add?

options.text: Choose one format and use it consistently.
options.explanation: Right. Mixing formats for the same purpose makes the structure harder to read.

options.text: Always use both formats, for every single section.
options.explanation: The guide says to choose one and use it consistently.

options.text: Tags only work for Claude models.
options.explanation: Gemini and OpenAI also recommend XML-style tags.

questions.prompt: Your prompt includes a 50k-token report and a question. Where do the Claude docs say the question should go?

options.text: At the end, after the report.
options.explanation: Right. The docs say queries at the end can improve quality by up to 30 percent in tests.

options.text: At the start, before the report.
options.explanation: The docs advise placing long documents near the top, above the query.

questions.prompt: The OpenAI docs say to place content you reuse in every request at the beginning of the prompt. Why?

options.text: To get the most cost and latency savings from prompt caching.
options.explanation: Right. Caching works on a repeated prefix.

options.text: Because the model ignores the second half of a prompt.
options.explanation: The model reads the whole context. The reason given is caching.

options.text: Because the API requires the system rules to be under 100 tokens.
options.explanation: There is no such limit. The reason given is caching.
